Case Study: Stepped Electricity Tariff

Read the passage carefully, then answer the 5 MCQs in the test below.

The State Electricity Board bills domestic users on a two-slab tariff. For the first 200 units of energy consumed in a month the charge builds up along one straight-line rule, and for every unit beyond 200 a steeper rule takes over. A consumer's monthly charge in rupees is modelled by f(x)=6x+150 for 0≤ x≤ 200 and f(x)=9x+k for x>200, where x is the number of units used and k is a constant fixed by the board. Customers complained that in an earlier scheme the bill jumped abruptly the moment usage crossed 200 units. To keep the tariff fair, the board now wants the two pieces to meet exactly at 200 units, so that a customer using slightly more than 200 units pays only slightly more — in other words, the charge function must be continuous at x=200.
